title: Pomelo Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Pomelo Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Pomelo nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and magnesium in suha, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Pomelo nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your suha (pomelo) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, zinc, phosphorus and boron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, magnesium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc and boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which pomelo nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Pomelo nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of suha

Young leaves mottled yellow between green veins, small, narrow and upright.

Small, hard, lumpy fruit with gum spots in the thick white peel. Many fruit drop. Shoot tips die.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a pomelo nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest pomelo nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in pomelo

No pomelo particular leaf description was found, so this follows the citrus pattern. Older leaves turn pale green, then yellow, evenly with no clear pattern, and drop early, so the canopy thins. New leaves are small, thin and light green, flushes are short, and the tree flowers sparsely and sets a light crop. You see it most at this stage: flowering and after harvest. A leaf survey of Mekong Delta pomelo orchards found nitrogen among the most limiting nutrients at both stages.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in suha
Trees fed little or irregularly, sandy or leached soils, heavy rain, waterlogging. Raw straw or manure that ties nitrogen up as it rots.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also yellows older leaves but leaves a green V at the leaf base and is worst next to the fruit. Sulfur deficiency starts on young leaves. To be sure, leaf test: the Mekong Delta study sampled the third and fourth leaves from 3 month old branches. Use 4 to 6 month old leaves from twigs without fruit.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply nitrogen in the weeded ring, split into two equal doses: when the rains begin, to build vigour before flowering. Again as the rainy months draw to a close. The guide budgets urea, complete fertilizer, muriate of potash and chicken dung every year, with the amount based on the soil analysis. For quick greening, give a Urea spray at 2 percent (20 grams per liter) every 15 days for citrus.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize every year by the soil test, ring weed before each dose and mulch.
Potassium deficiency in pomelo

Leaf signs follow citrus: the edges of older leaves turn pale yellow or bronze, then the yellow spreads, and new leaves are small. In pomelo the cost shows most in the crop. In a trial on 13 year old Magallanes pomelo in Davao City, trees given more potash flowered about four times as much, set 86 to 117 percent more fruit, carried about seven times as many fruit. Had heavier fruit with thinner peel and more juice. You see it most at this stage: flowering, fruit set and the first two months of fruit growth. In the Davao trial peak flowering and fruit set came in April and peak flushing in June.
Why potassium deficiency happens in suha
Sandy or leached soils, heavy rain, soils rich in magnesium, and nitrogen fed without enough potash. While each heavy crop carries potash away.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also starts on older leaves, but leaves a green V at the base. Salt or fertilizer burn scorches edges on leaves of all ages. To be sure, leaf test of the third and fourth leaves from 3 month old branches, and a soil test for potash, magnesium and calcium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

In the Davao trial the recommended rate was 150 grams of potassium (K) per tree as a basal dose, about 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60. 225 grams of potassium per tree (about 450 grams of Muriate of potash) gave much more flowering, fruit set and yield. Adding a foliar potash spray to the basal dose helped further. Time the doses before flowering and in the two months after fruit set.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash every year along with nitrogen, and more on trees carrying heavy crops.
Magnesium deficiency in pomelo

Older and middle leaves yellow between the veins. As in other citrus, the yellow starts near the leaf base on each side of the midrib and spreads until only the tip and a V shaped area at the base stay green, then the leaf turns yellow to bronze and drops. Limbs carrying heavy fruit show it most. In a Chinese honey pomelo district, about a third of leaves showed this yellowing and most soils were short of magnesium. You see it most at this stage: fruit growth, on heavily bearing limbs.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in suha
Acid soils, especially soils acidified by years of heavy ammonium fertilizer, high rainfall that leaches magnesium, and heavy potash. Seedy fruit draw more magnesium than seedless kinds.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole tree evenly. Potassium deficiency bronzes the leaf edges. To be sure, leaf test and a soil test for pH, magnesium, potash and calcium.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

On acid soils use Dolomite. Aim for pH 5.5 to 6.5 and lime below pH 5. Where the soil test shows low magnesium, give magnesium at 20 percent of the nitrogen rate, as Magnesium sulfate or Kieserite. In the Chinese honey pomelo trial, sprays of Magnesium sulfate at 4 percent (40 grams per liter), about 7 liters per tree split over three monthly sprays, together with much less NPK, raised leaf magnesium and cut the yellowing. That is a strong mix, so try a few branches first.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime with dolomite, avoid overusing ammonium fertilizers, and keep potash and magnesium in balance.
Zinc deficiency in pomelo

No pomelo particular description was found, so this follows citrus. Young leaves show yellow patches between the veins with an uneven green band along the midrib and main veins (mottle leaf). In severe cases new leaves are small, narrow, pointed and upright, twigs die back. Fruit on weak twigs stay small with low juice. You see it most at this stage: new flushes.
Why zinc deficiency happens in suha
High pH and limed soils, heavy phosphate, heavy poultry manure, organic soils and cold wet spells.
How to tell it apart

Citrus greening (HLB) is the main look alike and, with tristeza, one of the main causes of low citrus production in the country. Do the pen test: zinc deficiency looks the same on both sides of the midrib, HLB blotches do not. To be sure, pen test, then a zinc spray on a few branches and a look at the next flush. If the mottle stays uneven, send leaves for an HLB laboratory test.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray zinc on each new flush when leaves are two thirds to almost fully expanded. Give Zinc sulfate at 2 percent (20 grams per liter) mixed with 1 percent lime (10 grams per liter) every two weeks for citrus. Zinc on the soil does not work on limey soils.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep the pH below 6.5, avoid heavy phosphate, include zinc in regular sprays, and control psyllids.
Phosphorus deficiency in pomelo

Leaf signs are weak and follow citrus: older leaves lose their deep green, partly yellow. May show a dull bronze or purplish cast with small freckles along the main veins. Flowering and fruit set are poor, leaves and fruit drop early, and fruit are coarse, with a hollow core and sour juice. A leaf survey of Mekong Delta pomelo found phosphorus the most limiting nutrient at flowering, fruit growth and after harvest. You see it most at this stage: all through the cycle. Most felt at flowering and fruit set.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in suha
Strongly acid soils where iron and aluminium lock phosphorus up, limey soils, low organic matter, cold wet soil and weak roots.
How to tell it apart

A thick peel is not proof of phosphorus shortage: in the Davao Magallanes trial, trees given more potash grew a thinner peel. So low potash can thicken it too. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test of the third and fourth leaves from 3 month old branches.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply a phosphorus fertilizer by the soil test. Complete fertilizer belongs in the pummelo budget every year. Superphosphate suits soils of any pH, and warns against DAP (18 46 0) on alkaline soils. Lime soils below pH 5 so phosphorus stays available.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus in the planting hole, keep the pH at 5.5 to 6.5, and add compost or chicken dung.
Boron deficiency in pomelo

No pomelo particular deficiency description was found, so this follows citrus. Fruit stay small, hard and misshapen, with gum pockets and dark spots in the white inner peel and sometimes in the core, and many drop. The growing tip dies and the shoot branches out. Young leaves curl and their veins split and turn corky. You see it most at this stage: flowering to fruit growth, often after a long dry spell.
Why boron deficiency happens in suha
Sandy and alkaline soils low in organic matter, high nitrogen or calcium, drought, and fertilizers with no micronutrients.
How to tell it apart

Too much boron is a real risk in pomelo. In a Chinese field trial, 100 grams of borax per tree per year, split in two doses, caused toxicity: yellowing between the veins that starts at the leaf tip and moves to the base. To be sure, soil and leaf test for boron before adding any. The Chinese study treats soil boron below 0.5 mg per kg as short and above 5 mg per kg as toxic.
What to apply for boron deficiency
Give a Borax spray at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter) for citrus. Use boron on the soil or as a spray, never both. Keep soil doses small and only on soils that test low.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use fertilizers that carry micronutrients, keep organic matter up and water during dry spells.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any pomelo nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your suha needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Pomelo nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my suha leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: the whole tree pale green to yellow, old leaves falling early, thin canopy and few flowers. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in pomelo?
items.a: Apply nitrogen in the weeded ring, split into two equal doses: when the rains begin, to build vigour before flowering. Again as the rainy months draw to a close.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in pomelo?
items.a: In the Davao trial the recommended rate was 150 grams of potassium (K) per tree as a basal dose, about 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60. 225 grams of potassium per tree (about 450 grams of Muriate of potash) gave much more flowering, fruit set and yield.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes magnesium deficiency in pomelo?
items.a: On acid soils use Dolomite. Aim for pH 5.5 to 6.5 and lime below pH 5.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my suha lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the pomelo nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
